The main dietary sources of inosine are organ meats, spinach, and brewer's yeast.Inosine attracted attention as a performance-boosting dietary supplement in the 1970s.However, studies conducted in the 1990s have shown that inosine may not have any beneficial effects on athletic performance and cannot be used as an ergogenic aid.53 This was replicated by Starling et al.

54 In fact, in a study in weightlifters, inosine treatment led to an unfavorable increase in creatinine phosphokinase (CPK) and free fatty acids.55 However, in a recent study, 30 athletes practicing martial arts were able to improve their endurance and performance after a one-time ingestion of 1 g inosine.56 Other studies have used inosine as a means to increase the serum concentration of urate to optimal levels.Studies focusing on the protective properties of urate in neurodegenerative diseases (AD, PD, multiple sclerosis, ALS, etc) have shown that inosine ingestion up to 3 g/d for 2 years
